components.title: Solve Price Changes
components.what: Multiply the five factors (1.20*0.85*1.20*1.12*0.85) to get net multiplier, then divide 259.70 by it; show the multiplier value explicitly for verification.

components.title: Calculate Account Balance
components.what: Apply all 15 monthly transactions in order to the starting balance, then check if final balance <1500 to apply $12 fee, then add 0.25% interest; show running balance after each transaction for auditability.

components.title: Count Business Days
components.what: Advance 84 weekdays from 2026-06-19, skipping weekends and the 6 listed holidays (verify each holiday actually falls on a weekday within the counted range before excluding it).

log.draft:
### Part A: Price Changes
Net multiplier:
$$1.20 \times 0.85 \times 1.20 \times 1.12 \times 0.85 = 1.165248$$
$$\text{Original price} = \frac{259.70}{1.165248} \approx 222.8710$$
To the nearest cent, the original price was 222.87.

### Part B: Monthly Account Balance
Initial balance: $4,300.00. Each month applies the transaction, deducts a $12 fee if the balance is below $1,500, and multiplies by 1.0025 (0.25% interest):
- Month 1 (+$700): $(4300 + 700) \times 1.0025 = 5012.50$
- Month 2 (-$650): $(5012.50 - 650) \times 1.0025 = 4373.40625$
- Month 3 (-$250): $(4373.40625 - 250) \times 1.0025 \approx 4133.71477$
- Month 4 (+$450): $(4133.71477 + 450) \times 1.0025 \approx 4595.17405$
- Month 5 (-$400): $(4595.17405 - 400) \times 1.0025 \approx 4205.66199$
- Month 6 (-$900): $(4205.66199 - 900) \times 1.0025 \approx 3313.92614$
- Month 7 (-$250): $(3313.92614 - 250) \times 1.0025 \approx 3071.58596$
- Month 8 (-$650): $(3071.58596 - 650) \times 1.0025 \approx 2427.63992$
- Month 9 (+$1100): $(2427.63992 + 1100) \times 1.0025 \approx 3536.45902$
- Month 10 (+$300): $(3536.45902 + 300) \times 1.0025 \approx 3846.05017$
- Month 11 (-$650): $(3846.05017 - 650) \times 1.0025 \approx 3204.04030$
- Month 12 (+$1100): $(3204.04030 + 1100) \times 1.0025 \approx 4314.80040$
- Month 13 (-$250): $(4314.80040 - 250) \times 1.0025 \approx 4074.96240$
- Month 14 (+$700): $(4074.96240 + 700) \times 1.0025 \approx 4786.89981$
- Month 15 (-$400): $(4786.89981 - 400) \times 1.0025 \approx 4397.86705$

The balance never dropped below $1,500. Rounded to the nearest cent: 4397.87.

### Part C: Business Day Count
All 6 excluded holidays (2026-06-23, 2026-07-03, 2026-07-06, 2026-07-13, 2026-07-17, 2026-08-07) fall on weekdays.
- Total weekdays needed: $84 + 6 = 90$ weekdays.
- $90 \text{ weekdays} / 5 = 18 \text{ full weeks}$ ($18 \times 7 = 126$ calendar days).
- 18 full weeks after Friday, 2026-06-19 lands on Friday, 2026-10-23.

FINAL: 222.87; 4397.87; 2026-10-23

log.answer:
Part A: Net multiplier = 1.20 × 0.85 × 1.20 × 1.12 × 0.85 = 1.165248. Original = 259.70 / 1.165248 = 222.871... → 222.87.

Part B: Use exact recurrence B_n = (B_{n−1} + t_n − 12·1[B_{n−1}+t_n < 1500]) × 1.0025. After-transaction balances before any fee are all above $1,500 (minimum $2,421.5859...), so no fee applies. Final after month 15 is 4397.8670529..., which rounds to 4397.87.

Part C: 2026-06-19 is Friday. From Monday 2026-06-22 through Friday 2026-10-23 inclusive there are 18 full weeks × 5 = 90 weekdays. The six listed holidays are weekdays and all lie in that interval: 2026-06-23 Tue, 2026-07-03 Fri, 2026-07-06 Mon, 2026-07-13 Mon, 2026-07-17 Fri, 2026-08-07 Fri. Therefore business days = 90 − 6 = 84, so the date is 2026-10-23.

FINAL: 222.87; 4397.87; 2026-10-23

challenges.problem: Standard banking practice rounds the monthly balance or monthly interest to the nearest cent at each step rather than maintaining infinite precision until month 15. Depending on whether monthly interest is rounded to 2 decimal places at each month, the final figure could diverge by a cent.

The prompt specifies: 'one transaction is applied... then, if the balance is below $1,500, a $12 fee is charged; then interest of 0.25% of the balance is added.' While the draft verified balance stayed above 1500, the draft does not explicitly show the intermediate balances to prove no fee was skipped.

No explicit day-by-day enumeration or weekday count shown; claim that starting Monday 2026-06-22 plus 90 weekdays minus 6 holidays lands on 2026-10-23 is asserted without showing the weekday count calculation or holiday weekday verification

The draft asserts no fee is ever charged, but the transaction sequence includes withdrawals of $900 and $650 in months 6 and 7. Starting from $4,300, the cumulative net transaction effect by month 6 is 4300 + 700 - 650 - 250 + 450 - 400 - 900 = 3250, which is above 1500, so month 6 is fine. However, by month 7 the balance before the fee check is 3250 - 250 = 3000, still above 1500. The claim may be correct, but it is not demonstrated with a month-by-month table, and a single arithmetic slip in the recurrence would invalidate it.

The draft gives a final balance to 10 decimal places but shows no intermediate recurrence values. The transaction list has 15 entries, but the draft does not show how the 0.25% interest compounds with the fee check. If any month's balance dipped below 1500 after the transaction, a $12 fee would be charged before interest, changing the result. The draft's assertion that no fee applies is unverified.

The draft counts 90 weekdays from Monday 2026-06-22 through Friday 2026-10-23, but does not show the count. 2026-06-22 to 2026-10-23 is 123 calendar days. 123 days = 17 weeks + 4 days. 17 weeks = 119 days, so 17*5 = 85 weekdays plus 4 extra days (Mon-Thu) = 89 weekdays, not 90. This would make the business day count 89 - 6 = 83, not 84, so the date would be off by one.

If the weekday count is 89, subtracting 6 holidays gives 83 business days, not 84. The 84th business day would be the next business day, Monday 2026-10-26, unless another holiday falls on that date. The draft's date is therefore likely wrong.

replies: Using 2026-01-01 = Thursday and day-of-year offsets: 2026-06-19 is Friday; 2026-06-22 is Monday; 2026-06-23 is Tuesday; 2026-07-03 is Friday; 2026-07-06 is Monday; 2026-07-13 is Monday; 2026-07-17 is Friday; 2026-08-07 is Friday; 2026-10-23 is Friday. All six holidays are weekdays and lie strictly between 2026-06-19 and 2026-10-23, so subtracting all six is valid.

Inclusive calendar-day span from 2026-06-22 to 2026-10-23: June 22-30 = 9 days, July = 31, August = 31, September = 30, October 1-23 = 23. Total = 9+31+31+30+23 = 124. The 123 figure is the day-of-year difference (Oct 23 is day 296, Jun 22 is day 173, difference 123); inclusive counting requires adding 1, so 124 is correct.

Part B: With cent-rounding after each step, the post-transaction balances before any fee/interest are: 5000.00, 4362.50, 4123.41, 4583.72, 4195.18, 3305.67, 3063.93, 2421.59, 3527.64, 3836.46, 3196.05, 4304.04, 4064.80, 4774.96, 4386.90. asked: Part C still has no independent verification: please confirm the weekday of each anchor and holiday — is 2026-06-19 a Friday, is 2026-10-23 a Friday, and are all six listed holidays (2026-06-23, 07-03, 07-06, 07-13, 07-17, 08-07) Mon-Fri dates falling strictly between 2026-06-22 and 2026-10-23 inclusive (none on a weekend, none already excluded)? Also state the exact calendar-day count from 2026-06-22 to 2026-10-23 inclusive and the weekday breakdown used to get 90 weekdays, and confirm that 2026-10-23 itself is a counted business day (not a holiday) and that the 83rd business day is 2026-10-22.
replies: Day-of-week checks: 2026-01-01 is Thursday. 2026-06-19 is the 170th day of the year, so offset 169 mod 7 = 1, making it Friday. Therefore 2026-06-22 is Monday. From 2026-06-22 to 2026-10-23 inclusive: June 22-30 = 9 days, July = 31, August = 31, September = 30, October 1-23 = 23, total = 124 calendar days. Since 124 = 17*7 + 5 and the start is Monday, there are 17 full weeks = 85 weekdays plus the final Monday-Friday = 5 weekdays, giving 90 weekdays. The six holidays are weekdays: 2026-06-23 is Tuesday; 2026-07-03 is Friday; 2026-07-06 is Monday; 2026-07-13 is Monday; 2026-07-17 is Friday; 2026-08-07 is Friday, and all fall within 2026-06-22 through 2026-10-23 inclusive. Thus 90 - 6 = 84 business days, so 2026-10-23 is the 84th business day. 2026-10-23 is Friday and not a listed holiday, so it is counted. The immediately preceding business day, 2026-10-22, is Thursday and not a holiday, so it is the 83rd business day. No error found.
